content:
Exponents questions are the fastest marks on an IMO paper — every one of them yields to five laws. Students lose those marks only when they mix the laws up under time pressure. Take the free IMO Class 7 Exponents and Powers online test below. It has 10 Olympiad-pattern MCQs with instant scoring. Every answer comes with a worked explanation. Aim for 8 out of 10.

What the IMO asks from Exponents and Powers in Class 7

  • The laws: aᵐ × aᵑ, aᵐ ÷ aᵑ, (aᵐ)ᵑ.
  • Zero and negative-style reasoning: a⁰ = 1.
  • Expressing large numbers in standard (scientific) form.
  • Comparing powers like 2³⁰ vs 3²⁰.
  • Unit-digit and last-digit patterns.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Multiply same bases: ADD exponents. 3⁴ × 3² = 3⁶, never 9⁶.
  • Power of a power: MULTIPLY. (10²)³ = 10⁶ = 1,000,000.
  • Any non-zero number to the power 0 equals 1 — even 999⁰.
  • Standard form: 149,600,000 km = 1.496 × 10⁸ km.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Multiplying base AND exponent for (5 × 2³)²-type questions.
  • Writing 2³ = 6 (it is 8 — repeated multiplication, not multiplication by 3).
  • Adding exponents when the BASES differ.

questions.explanation: Product rule: a^(m) × aⁿ = a^(m+n) — keep the base, add the exponents. 4 + 2 + 1 = 7, so the answer is 3⁷.

questions.q: Express (10²)³ in exponential form and give its value.
Find the value of x if 2^(x+1) = 8².

questions.explanation: Move the decimal point 5 places right: 4.5. Moving right means a negative exponent: 4.5 × 10⁻⁵.
Move the decimal 10 places right to reach 2.05. Result: 2.05 × 10⁻¹⁰.
Make the exponents equal: 2³⁰ = (2³)¹⁰ = 8¹⁰ and 3²⁰ = (3²)¹⁰ = 9¹⁰. Since 9 > 8, we get 9¹⁰ > 8¹⁰, so 3²⁰ is larger.
